sources.name: Unicode CLDR
sources.version: 48.0 (as shipped in ICU 78.3 with Node 22.23.4; plural rules compared with cldr-json main on 2026-11-11)

provenance.notes: Written in this phase from the cited references and re-expressed; the Arabic text is the researcher's own wording and needs a native reviewer. The checks are proposals for the harness, not yet run.

title.ar: العملة ظاهرة دائمًا وباسم يفهمه القارئ
title.en: The currency is always shown, in a form the reader understands

statement.ar: لا تعرض مبلغًا بلا عملة حيث يمكن أن توجد أكثر من عملة. في الواجهة العربية استخدم الرمز العربي المعتمد للعملة («ج.م»، «ر.س») أو اسمها، واستخدم رمز ISO حيث يلزم التمييز بين عملات تتشابه رموزها.
statement.en: Do not show an amount without its currency where more than one currency is possible. In an Arabic interface use the currency's established Arabic symbol ("ج.م", "ر.س") or its name, and the ISO code where currencies with similar symbols must be told apart.

rationale.ar: «ريال» و«دينار» و«جنيه» أسماء تشترك فيها عملات عدة بقيم مختلفة جدًا.
rationale.en: "Riyal", "dinar" and "pound" are names shared by several currencies of very different values.

checks: Every rendered money value has a currency symbol, code or name within the same isolated unit or in the column header.
A currency field shows its currency beside the input, outside the editable text (amounts-harvested CI-F13: a symbol typed inside is rejected).
The Arabic symbol comes from currency data, not a literal in a component.
